findings.observation: No complete-scene benchmark has a current independent visual review and maintainer sign-off. Prior parity prose and passing technical gates are not that approval.
findings.acceptance: Review the desktop/phone, day/night benchmark in motion against pinned reference footage; resolve its defects, record all rubric verdicts and obtain an explicit maintainer decision.

findings.observation: In the desktop daylight plate view, the grass is broad saturated bands, the fence is a uniform green panel with repeated yellow posts, and the distant houses read as simple colored silhouettes. The reference plate view layers visible grass variation, built facades, shrubs, flowers and fence construction. Our setting reads markedly less finished.
evidence: BB2026 local reference corpus: steam/steam-02.jpg (see docs/research/backyard-2026-reference.md)
findings.acceptance: Build and review a cohesive Parks Dept #2 material and environment pass with readable ground variation, fence construction, layered vegetation and recognizable architectural detail at both review sizes; retain clear ball silhouettes and existing draw/triangle budgets.

findings.observation: In the desktop daylight plate view, large grey faceted cloud slabs occupy the upper frame and compete with the colorful neighborhood. Their blocky, dark treatment is visually inconsistent with the softer bright sky in the pinned reference.
evidence: BB2026 local reference corpus: steam/steam-02.jpg (see docs/research/backyard-2026-reference.md)
findings.acceptance: Review the cloud silhouette, shading and sky composition from plate, field and deep cameras in day and night; establish a coherent cartoon sky without distracting dark slabs or horizon artifacts.

findings.observation: The benchmark batter looks toward the catcher rather than the incoming pitch. bridge.ts places every batter at a root yaw of PI; the delivered stance does not compensate for it. A production-factory/director diagnostic of all 30 delivered models at stance times 0, 0.5 and 1 seconds finds head-forward dot toward pitcher negative in all 90 samples. This is a shared world-space orientation defect, not only Junebug. Correction implemented in the batting-fix proposal with a 5,040-frame delivered-roster sweep and refreshed evidence; remains open pending independent visual review and maintainer sign-off.
findings.acceptance: Correct the integrated plate orientation, then verify all 30 delivered characters look toward the incoming pitch throughout ready/load and swing across the plate. Rerun audit:batting -- --check, capture production plate views and continuous swings at desktop/phone sizes, and independently review shoulder/feet/head orientation and contact. A positive direction metric alone is insufficient.

findings.observation: Junebug holds the handle behind the torso with an open trailing hand rather than a readable two-handed batting grip in the benchmark (frames 0 and 75). Existing groundContact coverage checks generic hand-bone proximity, not delivered palm/finger contact with the handle through motion. The diagnostic records bone-to-bat-axis offsets; these are not a measured mesh gap or a validated grip score. Correction implemented in the batting-fix proposal with a 5,040-frame delivered-roster sweep and refreshed evidence; remains open pending independent visual review and maintainer sign-off.
evidence: src/v2/render/groundContact.test.ts:bat_stance keeps both hands on the one bat it holds
findings.acceptance: Review and correct the delivered hand/arm/prop relationship through ready, load, contact, follow-through and recovery. Show both hands plausibly enclosing the handle, sensible wrist/elbow bends, no body/bat penetration, and the barrel meeting the actual ball at contact. Sweep every delivered character for the same defect before resolving its scope; add regressions for measurable relationships without substituting bone proximity for visual approval.

findings.observation: The earlier character inventory could be complete without an in-game batting-ready/load/contact/follow view or per-character pitching, throwing, pickup, dive and slide motion. The expanded generated matrix makes these missing checks visible. No claim is made that uninspected cells are defective or passed.
findings.acceptance: Capture and inspect every generated character/action slot at both review sizes. Record observed failures in this ledger, including exact clip/phase/time and affected ids; retain unreviewed cells as incomplete. Fix one cause at a time and rerun the affected roster and adjacent transitions before an independent review and maintainer verdict.

findings.observation: The September 18 live review at 1280x720 found Junebug presenting a side profile in the draft after the batting-pose correction, with waiting kids stacked behind the candidate. Walk-off facing also opposed the direction of travel. The parity-review branch corrects clip-aware facing and separates the waiting group; this is an implementation proposal, not independent visual approval.
findings.acceptance: Review the entrance, held pose, confirmation and walk to both benches for all hero-pose families at desktop and phone sizes; faces must address the viewer and the chosen child must be identifiable without reading the name. Record fresh evidence before independent review and sign-off.

findings.observation: The draft pairs a green-shirted illustrated Junebug portrait with a red-clothed 3D Junebug. The custom captain also differs markedly between portrait and stage. Two individually recognizable depictions are not a consistent visual identity; a child choosing by appearance may not recognize the same kid in play.
findings.acceptance: Use approved depictions that agree on silhouette, face, hair and signature clothing across title, selection card, team tray and live model. Review every roster identity and custom-player combination without altering v1 art or preference tallies.

findings.observation: The live review of seed critical-review in the wide field camera showed the rectangular turf boundary against the sky and a ball that was barely distinguishable from a single bright speck. The distance-based ball cue reaches its scale cap before the deep camera can preserve readable pixels. The parity-review branch extends the same turf mesh through the horizon and applies a viewport-aware minimum live-ball diameter. The proposal passes technical projection/geometry tests and presentation smoke; motion comparison and independent visual review remain open.
findings.acceptance: Show a continuous ground-to-horizon composition through field/deep camera moves and a ball that remains clearly identifiable at desktop and landscape-phone sizes, without changing physical ball size, collision, catches or input tolerance. Compare fresh full-scene motion and retain performance budgets.
